translit: mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo ’stvakarmaṇi
theme: Do your work, let go of the result
hindi: तुम्हारा अधिकार केवल कर्म करने में है, उसके फलों में कभी नहीं। इसलिए कर्म के फल को अपना उद्देश्य मत बनाओ, और कर्म न करने में भी तुम्हारा मन न लगे।
english: You have a right only to your work, never to its results. Don’t let the results be your reason for acting — and don’t become attached to doing nothing either.
deeper: Krishna separates two things that we usually mix together: effort, which is fully in our hands, and result, which depends on many things we can’t control — other people, timing, health, luck, and God’s will.

When we keep staring at the result, two troubles come: fear (“what if I fail?”) and greed (“I must get the prize”). Both shake the mind, and a shaky mind actually works worse. A calm mind that is fully inside the work does its best.

But Krishna closes the escape door too: “Then why do anything at all?” — no. Running away from work out of fear is also wrong. The ideal is to give your full heart to the work, offer the result to God, and accept whatever comes with a steady mind. This is called Karma Yoga.
background: The armies of the Pandavas and Kauravas stand facing each other at Kurukshetra. Arjuna asks Krishna, his charioteer, to place the chariot between the two armies. There he sees his grandfather Bhishma, his teacher Drona, cousins and friends — all ready to fight.

His body trembles, his bow Gandiva slips from his hand, and he sits down saying, “I will not fight” (2.9). Krishna first teaches him that the soul never dies (2.11–30), then reminds him of his duty as a warrior (2.31–38). Then, in verse 2.39, Krishna says, “Now hear the wisdom of yoga — the art of acting well.” Verse 2.47 is the heart of that teaching.
lessons: Fall in love with the process.
The prize is one day; the practice is every day. Enjoy the practice.
Spend your energy where your control is.
Worrying about the result uses up energy that your effort needed.
Failure is feedback, not the end.
If the result is not yours, then a bad result doesn’t define you either.
Doing nothing is also a choice.
Avoiding work out of fear is the trap Krishna warns about.
Work done with love becomes worship.
Offer your best to God and let Him take care of the rest.
examples: Riya studies with full focus for one hour every day, without thinking “Will I get 100?” In the exam her mind is calm, and she writes well.
Aarav got out after scoring just 5 runs. He didn’t throw his bat — the next day he was back at the nets, practising.
Meera didn’t win a prize, but she painted with her whole heart and learned a new shading technique. Learning is the real win.
Kabir sowed a seed and watered it every day. He can’t make it grow overnight — his job is only to water it.
Ananya plays the harmonium every day, whether anyone claps or not. Slowly her fingers start moving on their own.
Simran didn’t want to enter the race because she was afraid of losing. The Gita says giving up action out of fear isn’t right either. She ran — and had a great time.
Arjun helps his mother put the dishes away — not for a chocolate reward, but because it’s his home too.
Ishaan posted a video and started checking his likes every five minutes. Then he decided: “My job is to make a good video. Likes are the result.”

story.title: Grandpa’s Mango Tree
paras: In a small village, eighty-year-old Ramdin Dadaji was planting a tiny mango sapling. Chintu, the ten-year-old boy next door, laughed. “Dadaji, a mango tree takes ten or twelve years to give fruit. By then you…” and he stopped.
Dadaji smiled. “Son, the tree whose mangoes you eat today was planted by my grandfather. He never tasted a single one of its fruits, yet he watered it with all his heart.”
Chintu asked, “Then what will you get?” Dadaji said, “I get the joy of planting it. Who gets the fruit, and when — that is for God to decide. My job is to plant it well and water it every day.”

That day, Chintu picked up a bucket too. Twelve years later, when the first mangoes appeared on the tree, Dadaji was no longer there. Chintu shared the first mango with the village children — and planted a new sapling right next to it.
story.moral: Lesson: Do your work with your whole heart; leave the fruit to time and to God.

quiz.q: According to this verse, what do we have a right to?
quiz.x: “Karmaṇy evādhikāras te” — your right is only to your action.

quiz.q: Who gave this teaching, and to whom?
quiz.x: Krishna taught the Gita to Arjuna on the chariot at Kurukshetra.

quiz.q: Someone stops studying because they’re afraid of failing. According to the Gita, this is…
o: Right — results aren’t in our hands anyway
Wrong — don’t be attached to inaction
Not related to the Gita at all
quiz.x: “Mā te saṅgo ’stv akarmaṇi” — don’t be attached to not acting.
Akarmaṇi means “in not acting,” or inaction.

reel.hook: Scared of failing? Krishna has a secret for you.
reel.lesson: Give your best; leave the result to God.
reel.caption:
Do your best, and let go of the worry 🏹
Today’s verse is one of the most famous lines of the Gita.
